My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift across the three horizons, anchored by the assumption that the asset or indicator in question was trading near 132–133 at the time of the forecast. For the one-day estimate of 132.5, I leaned heavily on short-term momentum and mean-reversion tendencies, expecting very little net movement over a single session. The one-week estimate of 133.0 incorporates a slight positive drift, consistent with a mildly bullish near-term trend or slightly positive carry, while the one-month estimate of 134.5 assumes that the same gradual upward pressure continues to compound without a major trend reversal. The step-up in point estimates is deliberately modest because I did not have strong conviction about a directional catalyst over any of these horizons.

The confidence interval widths widen considerably as the horizon extends, which reflects the basic statistical reality that uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the 90% interval of roughly plus or minus 2.7 around the point estimate is narrow because intraday and overnight volatility for most liquid assets is constrained by market microstructure and liquidity. At one week, the interval widens to plus or minus 6, capturing the possibility of a meaningful macro data release, earnings announcement, or sentiment shift that could move prices more substantially. At one month, the interval of 122 to 147 — a range of 25 points — reflects the full suite of risks that can materialize over four weeks, including central bank decisions, geopolitical developments, and shifts in broader risk appetite.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside even these relatively wide intervals. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic conditions — such as a hotter-than-expected inflation print triggering aggressive rate hike expectations, or a credit event in a major economy — could push the one-month realization well below 122. A liquidity crisis or sharp risk-off episode could amplify moves that would otherwise seem unlikely. On the upside, a surprisingly dovish policy pivot, a major positive earnings surprise, or a geopolitical resolution that reduces uncertainty premiums could push the outcome above 147. These tail scenarios are by definition not fully captured in a 90% interval, and they tend to arrive with little warning.

Finally, I want to be transparent that these estimates carry meaningful model uncertainty on top of the stated probabilistic uncertainty. The point estimates and intervals are constructed from a combination of trend extrapolation, historical volatility scaling, and qualitative judgment about near-term risks — not from a deeply calibrated quantitative model with a long out-of-sample track record.
